- When sentiment is predominantly negative (-1.00) over recent days, model tends to underpredict true prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to account for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward; reduce forecast dip by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward prior 5–10 day average, model tends to overpredict or underpredict; align forecast with 7-day moving average for smoother correction.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa), model lags in adjusting; delay forecast shift by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price in early-to-mid period; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 7–10 days to capture short-term volatility.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 patterns, model often misaligns with true trend; use sentiment-weighted average (e.g., 60% recent, 40% prior) to smooth forecast drift.
